recipes.name: Beer Batter Deep Fried Dill Pickles
ingredients_raw: 1 (12 fluid ounce) can or bottle beer

steps.text: Heat oil in a deep-fryer or large saucepan to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C). Whisk together the beer, 1 1/2 cups flour, pepper, garlic powder, chili powder, and seasoned salt in a large bowl. Dip the pickle slices into the beer batter, then coat them in the remaining 1 1/2 cups flour.
Fry the pickles in the preheated oil until golden and crisp, about 5 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Beer Batter Deep Fried Dill Pickles
raw_recipe.description: Beer makes everything taste better. Serve these tasty, fried pickle slices as an appetizer or snack at your next event.

review.reviewBody: These are unbelievably good. I fell in love with fried pickles at the AllRecipes Southern Round up in Florida. I never thought that I would be able to make these better than the ones that I had there but this recipe does it. I was a little worried when reading the recipe beccause I always dredged my food in the flour first, then in the beer batter. This recipe calls for just the opposite. So, I compromised, I dredged in the flour then in the batter and then again in the flour. I cannot believe how crispy this batter was. Even after sitting on the table for 30 minutes or so the breading was incredibly crisp. I am going to try using this recipe on fish and shrimp to see if it will remain crisp. This is definitely my go to fried pickle recip from now on. Thank you so much for posting.

Made these at my local bar (easier to use their fryer than do at home). They disappeared like smoke. I use a little less flour (1 bottle beer to 1 cup flour) to make a slightly thinner batter, as I like to use sandwhich slices (stackers) as opposed to quarters.

I had never had a fried pickle. My husband asked me to make "fried dill pickles." Huh? Well ....ok... After reading the reviews I made this recipe with equal parts beer and flour. ( I made it with one cup beer and one cup flour.) The seasonings were kept the same as written except I added a pinch of cayenne pepper. I did use sandwich slice dills and drained them on a paper towels as to decrease the spattering of oil. I suggest using the refrigerated (cold packed) dill pickles like Claussen or store brand of that nature. (Just because they turned out soooo good!) My husband requested thousand island dressing as the dip .. ( ketchup, mayo and pickle relish) He said to "Save that recipe!" I'm betting this batter would make great onion rings.
I doubled the amount of seasoning and added cayenne pepper! I put some seasoning in the dry flour as well and it was absolutely delicious! These are the best fried pickles I've had!

These are good Tinita, thank you. But I still prefer my simpler version of this. Equal parts beer and flour and seasonings of choice. Mix and let sit for 10 minutes or so. This creates a tempura like batter. Also, to make it less messy and easier, you can lightly dredge your pickles in cornstarch prior to dipping in batter.
Great recipe. I drained the pickles and dried them with a paper towel before breading and frying. The pickles were juicy and the coating was crispy!

Love this recipe, incredibly easy to throw together. I used Guinness Blonde Ale as my beer; I find that using a beer with a stronger flavor helps the batter stand out a lot more. I would recommend for this recipe, having more than a cup and a half of flour on standby for use after dipping the pickle slices in the batter you've made before frying them. That set of flour tends to get a little tacky and makes it harder for the batter to adhere to the pickles.

All in all, awesome recipe. I substituted seasoned salt with garlic salt, (and yes, I still added the garlic powder haha) and after they were done frying I draped a pinch of plain salt over them just for flavor. Love it. Thank you so much for this recipe. Plan on trying a variation of it for fish and chips shortly.

Also, to those of you nay-sayers who say that it makes too much batter and it becomes runny; the key to any beer batter is to slowly add the beer in while whisking it after you've added all the powdered ingredients together. As soon as the batter loses its lumpy consistency, you're ready to go. Any more than that and it will, of course, be runny.

I can't find my cookbook where I saved the recipe for beer batter that I usually use. Came across this one and liked that it did not require eggs. I cut it in half & eyeballed spice amounts, but it came out great! Used it to deep-fry dill pickles slices, as well as stuffed zucchini blossoms & fresh green beans. YUM! (Stuffed zucchini blossoms with leftover vegan herbed mashed potatoes.)

We dipped the pickles in flour first, then batter and flour again. Absolutely amazing. We also used dill and regular cheese curds and it was delicious!! Highly recommend this recipe for any deep frying adventures! Cheese curds fried in a about a minute and a half -- definitely try making these!

I used a sweet & spicy dill pickle. I would recommend using canola oil. I also used a fryer. I had some difficulty with the first batch ( stuck together). I would add 1 T of cornstarch to the batter. Great taste!
Needs more flavor. Makes way too much batter. Batter needs to be thicker.

I made this a few years ago and I had to go back and find the recipe to make it again. I couldn't remember where I found it, but I thought about this page, and here we are making it again. It's so good! Chef Kenneth Hare
The best fried pickles I have ever tasted!

This recipe is super easy to follow—easy enough that you probably won’t have to look at it again just one or two times after making it. It’s also delicious (the brand/type of pickle used is a factor in this as well, of course). For those reasons alone I would give it 5 stars! 

I reduced my rating to 4 stars because an entire 12 ounce beer makes the batter too runny. Instead of following the batter measurements to a T, I use my best judgement to get what I believe is the perfect consistency.

Easy and good. These were easy to make, and were eaten up in about 30mins.. 

I used the whole 24oz jar to make them, and this recipe was still plenty of batter and flour.
It turned out great except the batter could have had a lot more flavour. Held a lot of grease.
I made these as the recipe states, but next time I think I will add more spices.

This recipe and batter was great. Once I got everything ready the fry up was very quick. I also fried fresh sliced jalapenos as well using the same recipe and they were incredibly good as well. Definitely keeping this one saved.

I followed the recipe and it was very good., My family loved it, The seasoning was also perfect! I didn't have regular salt so I used seasoned salt and it worked out fine! I just need a good dip recipe now!

I felt they needed a little more flavor. I loved the crispness of the pickles but it was kind of bland. I didn't finish the batch last night because I wasn't impressed. Today I decided to change it up just a little and they were 5 star. I took the left over wet batter and added a touch of Kentucky Kernel seasoned flour and dipped them in KK as well instead of just AP flour. Next time I'll just use the KK instead of AP flour.
